item.title: NYPD body camera footage shows aftermath of ICE agent shooting in Marble Hill
item.description: Oscar Bergal, 28, was shot once in the neck by an ICE agent who fired shots at his car Thursday afternoon, according to authorities.

item.title: Panama struck by magnitude 7.7 earthquake, U.S. Geological Survey says
item.description: A powerful magnitude 7.7 earthquake has struck Panama, shaking buildings in the capital and prompting evacuations.

item.title: Trump promised to lower prices for Americans. Here's what the data shows.
item.description: Just weeks before the midterm elections, 90% of Americans say prices in the U.S. are the main factor shaping their view of the economy. These charts show why.

item.title: Trump announces Russia will release millions of tons of diesel to help with costs
item.description: Russian President Vladimir Putin agreed to release 300,000 tons of diesel immediately and millions more over the coming months.

item.title: Watch: Florida Gov. Ron DeSantis speaks on Hurricane Isaias preparations
item.description: Florida Gov. Ron DeSantis held a news briefing on Friday hours ahead of Hurricane Isaiah's expected landfall as a Category 3 storm. DeSantis laid out preparation plans and more.

item.title: Thieves steal 30,000 bottles of wine in Italy's largest-ever heist
item.description: The theft targeted the Marchesi Antinori winery near Cortona, in the province of Arezzo, the company said.

item.title: Philadelphia police say Anthropic AI submitted a "false homicide tip"
item.description: Anthropic notified the Philadelphia Police Department of the incident on Oct. 7 and plans to publish a report describing what happened.

item.title: Durbin asks watchdog to probe new FBI hiring standards on bestiality, prostitution
item.description: Sen. Dick Durbin asked the DOJ's watchdog to investigate why the FBI lowered its hiring standards for candidates who may have engaged in bestiality, prostitution or employment theft.

item.title: Hurricane Isaias becomes Category 3 storm as it threatens northern Gulf Coast
item.description: Hurricane Isaias, the first Atlantic hurricane of 2026, is inching closer to the northern Gulf Coast, where it is expected to make landfall on Friday evening.

item.title: These documents tell the story of the Cornell rape allegations
item.description: Hundreds of pages of documents obtained by CBS News detail Jane Doe's allegations, the Cornell police investigation and responses of some of the accused Chi Phi fraternity members.

item.title: Top Trump aide's daughter photographed with pro-Russia politician in Bosnia
item.description: Katie Wiles, the daughter of White House chief of staff Susie Wiles, recently traveled to Republika Srpska, the Bosnian-controlled territory led by pro-Russian Serb Milorad Dodik. CBS News' Emmett Lyons explains more.

item.title: Trump picks Katie Zacharia as next White House press secretary
item.description: Katie Zacharia, a conservative commentator, has been offered the role of White House press secretary, a White House official told CBS News on Friday.

item.title: Bodycam footage shows moments after ICE shooting in NYC
item.description: A man was shot by a U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement agent in New York City. The NYPD released body camera footage showing the moment police officers responded to the scene.

item.title: Only 2 other countries hold public executions as U.S. plans first in 90 years
item.description: The execution of Nidal Hasan, convicted in the 2009 killings of 13 people at Fort Hood, will be livestreamed, the Defense Department said.

item.title: Mike Ditka, former Chicago Bears head coach, dies at 86
item.description: Raised in a blue-collar Pennsylvania town, Mike Ditka earned a scholarship to Pitt and became "Da Coach" in Chicago. His family called him "the heart of our family" in announcing his death at 86.

item.title: Iran's Houthi allies step up deadly attacks on Saudi Arabia
item.description: Saudi Arabia says missile strikes by Iran's Houthi allies killed three people at Riyadh's airport as fighting escalates in the Middle East conflict's new epicenter.

item.title: Vance says he wouldn't watch livestream of Fort Hood shooter's execution
item.description: Vice President JD Vance cast doubt on whether the Pentagon will go ahead with livestreaming the execution of the Fort Hood shooter and said he would not tune in if it happens.

item.title: Nobel Peace Prize awarded to former ICC judge Navi Pillay
item.description: Nobel Peace Prize 2026 was awarded to Navanethem "Navi" Pillay, a former judge on the International Criminal Court, drawing a quick, angry rebuke from Israel.

item.title: FBI arrests suspected member of ShinyHunters in connection with jobs site hack
item.description: The FBI this week arrested another individual suspected of being connected to ShinyHunters, the cybercriminal group that hacked the bureau's job website, FBI Director Kash Patel said.

item.title: RFK Jr., Zeldin pressed by Democrats on possible roles in Trump pardons
item.description: Democratic lawmakers are pressing HHS Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. and EPA Administrator Lee Zeldin to explain what role they may have played in pardons granted by President Trump.

item.title: Pentagon's plan to livestream execution sparks backlash
item.description: "Public executions are what oppressive dictatorships like Iran and Afghanistan do," said GOP Sen. Thom Tillis.

item.title: Mike Ditka, who led Chicago Bears to only Super Bowl title, dies at 86
item.description: Legendary football coach Mike Ditka has died at age 86. CBS News Chicago's Matt Zahn reports.

item.title: U.S. measles cases top 4,000, far surpassing 2025 total, CDC says
item.description: The record number of measles cases in the U.S. so far this year has topped 4,000, the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention reported Friday.

item.title: Panama City "ready" for Hurricane Isaias, local official says
item.description: Panama City, Florida, city manager Jonathan Hayes shares how his city is preparing for Hurricane Isaias.

item.title: SpaceX says Starlink will "become a major mobile carrier in the U.S."
item.description: SpaceX said it has bought licenses for radio airwaves that will help its Starlink satellite business provide cellphone service across the U.S.

item.title: Maps and charts show record number of measles cases in U.S. this year
item.description: CBS News has been tracking a record number of measles cases and outbreaks around the country in 2026. The majority of cases are among those who haven't been vaccinated.

item.title: Guilfoyle associate says when she asked him for $100K, it was "quid pro quo"
item.description: White House officials were told that text messages between Kimberly Guilfoyle and Eric Deters were real, sources told CBS News.

item.title: Man shot by ICE agent in New York City's Marble Hill, authorities say
item.description: A man was hospitalized after being shot by an ICE agent in New York City's Marble Hill neighborhood, according to the DHS and city officials.

item.title: LAPD dog shootings raise questions about police tactics, practices
item.description: CBS California Investigates looked at the LAPD's Use of Force reports over the past 10 years and found the LAPD had 19 cases in which officers shot at dogs in 2016. So far in 2026, there have been four incidents, resulting in three deaths.

item.title: Jane Doe's account of what happened at Cornell fraternity house
item.description: A former Cornell student, identified as Jane Doe, filed a civil lawsuit against the school and seven former fraternity brothers she accuses of rape and sexual assault.
